Return one status per item, under its ref: SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE, with the page sentence you relied on.
Items, one per line:
p1:c1: The reference GISMo training command fixes the ingredient-encoder width at 300 dimensions (`hidden=300 emb_d=300`), with 2 GIN layers, 400 epochs and regular negative sampling — the single width the card would vary. | source: https://github.com/facebookresearch/gismo/blob/main/gismo/README.md | recorded quote: \"python train.py name=GIN_MLP setup=context-full max_context=43 \ lr=0.00005 w_decay=0.0001 hidden=300 emb_d=300 dropout=0.25 \ nr=400 nlayers=2 lambda_=0.0 i=1 init_emb=random \ with_titles=False with_set=True filter=False\"
p1:c2: GISMo's published Recipe1MSubs test result — MRR 31.51 and Hit@1 20.56, averaged over 5 runs — is the exact baseline the card's 'Check first' reproduction targets. | source: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2302.07960 | recorded quote: \"Table 1: Test results on Recipe1MSubs. Our method outperforms the baselines on all metrics. Results are averaged over 5 runs, and the mean ± std are reported. ... GISMo (Ours) 31.51±0.10 20.56±0.14 35.89±0.16 54.27±0.19\"
p1:c3: The model is implemented in PyTorch with the Deep Graph Library (DGL) for sparse graph operations, over a 6,653-ingredient FlavorGraph-derived vocabulary and the ~49k-pair Recipe1MSubs training split — the scale and tooling the card would reuse. | source: https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2302.07960 | recorded quote: \"We implement our model in PyTorch [44], and use deep graph library (DGL) [57] for the sparse operations. ... As a result, our ingredient vocabulary contains 6,653 ingredients.\"
p1:c4: The project is an archived, read-only open-source benchmark (Meta AI authors), not an actively developed product, and GISMo feeds a personalized inverse-cooking (image-to-recipe) pipeline. | source: https://github.com/facebookresearch/gismo | recorded quote: \"This repository was archived by the owner on Nov 1, 2024. It is now read-only.\"
p1:done: Meta only ever trained and evaluated GISMo at a single ingredient-encoder width (hidden=300, emb_d=300); the paper's 5-run average is at that one width and no 64–512 sweep exists in the paper or repo. | source: https://github.com/facebookresearch/gismo/blob/main/gismo/README.md | recorded quote: \"To train the best performing model, use this command in the gismo folder: python train.py name=GIN_MLP setup=context-full max_context=43 lr=0.00005 w_decay=0.0001 hidden=300 emb_d=300 dropout=0.25 nr=400 nlayers=2 lambda_=0.0 i=1 init_emb=random with_titles=False with_set=True filter=False\"
p2:c1: They re-implemented and re-ran GISMo as their benchmark, fixing the ingredient embedding dimension at 300 with two 300-hidden-unit graph convolutional layers, a dropout of 0.25, and 400 epochs with negative sampling. | source: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-4990/6/4/131 | recorded quote: \"We set the learning rate to 5 × 10−5, weight decay to 0.0001, and used an embedding dimension of 300 to represent ingredients in a continuous vector space. The model consists of two graph convolutional layers, each with 300 hidden units, and applies a dropout rate of 0.25 to reduce overfitting.\"
p2:c2: Their reimplemented GISMo baseline scores Hit@1 34.53 ± 0.10% on the original Recipe1MSubs, and fine-tuned GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 lifts this to 38.03 ± 0.28%, while TinyLlama-1.1B reaches only 20.93 ± 0.29%. | source: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-4990/6/4/131 | recorded quote: \"On the original and filtered dataset, the Hit@1 accuracy was 34.53 ± 0.10% and 40.24 ± 0.36%, respectively. ... Subsequent experiments with fine-tuned LLMs on the original GISMo ingredient substitution dataset yielded Hit@1 values of 20.09 ± 0.31% for DaVinci-002, 20.93 ± 0.29% for TinyLlama-1.1B, and 38.03 ± 0.28% for GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106.\"
p2:c3: The work sits inside the Hyperfoods ERC programme (coordinated by Imperial College London), which applies graph-based ML to computationally design personalised nutrition and which funded Rita et al. | source: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/899932 | recorded quote: \"Hyperfoods will use novel graph-based ML methods to provide the technological capabilities for the computational discovery and design of personalised nutrition.\"
p2:c4: The re-run GISMo and fine-tuned models (plus the dataset-filtering and fine-tuning scripts) are released on the iAnalytica Bitbucket repository, so the card's width-sweep could be reproduced against their released baseline. | source: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-4990/6/4/131 | recorded quote: \"the fine-tuned models GISMo and TinyLlama, along with the scripts used for filtering the Recipe1MSubs dataset and fine-tuning the GISMo, DaVinci, GPT-3.5, and TinyLlama models, are hosted on the Bitbucket repository.\"
p2:done: Rita et al. re-implemented GISMo at a single 300-dim embedding width (averaged over 5 runs) and swept model families (DaVinci/TinyLlama/GPT-3.5), but never swept the GISMo encoder width across 64–512. | source: https://www.mdpi.com/2504-4990/6/4/131 | recorded quote: \"used an embedding dimension of 300 to represent ingredients in a continuous vector space. The model consists of two graph convolutional layers, each with 300 hidden units\"

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
- Search the web using the session's web search provider - performs real-time web searches and can scrape content from specific URLs
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Supports configurable result counts and returns the content from the most relevant websites
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

Usage notes:
  - Supports live crawling modes when available: 'fallback' (backup if cached unavailable) or 'preferred' (prioritize live crawling)
  - Search types when available: 'auto' (balanced), 'fast' (quick results), 'deep' (comprehensive search)
  - Configurable context length for optimal LLM integration
  - Domain filtering and advanced search options available

The current year is 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information or current events
- Example: If the current year is 2026 and the user asks for "latest AI news", search for "AI news 2026", NOT "AI news 2025"

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 8)

livecrawl.description: Live crawl mode - 'fallback': use live crawling as backup if cached content unavailable, 'preferred': prioritize live crawling (default: 'fallback')

type.description: Search type - 'auto': balanced search (default), 'fast': quick results, 'deep': comprehensive search

contextMaxCharacters.description: Maximum characters for context string optimized for LLMs (default: 10000)
